newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates firmer at start of week.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates firmer at start of week.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were slightly firmer on Monday with liquidity remaining pretty high ahead of fortnightly reserve payments, a dealer said.
New settlements were put at 42.3 million kuna and supply of some 40 million was left unmet, a dealer said, because of lack of demand.
"Liquidity is good but not as good as last week," she said.
Call money, accounting for 35 million kuna of morning trade, stayed flat at 8.0 percent.
Term loans were higher, with one-month loans struck at 12 and 15 percent and two-month money fetching 18 percent, up from 16 percent on Friday.
On Friday night banks sought 2.7 million kuna to square their positions.
Saturday overnight trade totalled 14.5 million of which two million went to banks for maintenance of their mandatory reserves and the rest was sought by four banks with shortfalls.
